title: Comparison equivalence of universal oriented cones
statement: In the common universe u let X,Y,S,P,Q be categories of the stated size and let P,Q be Grothendieck topoi [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Let f:X→S, g:Y→S, p1:P→X,p2:P→Y,q1:Q→X,q2:Q→Y be geometric morphisms [def-trf-geometric-morphism], with orientations tau:(gp2)_*→(fp1)_* and sigma:(gq2)_*→(fq1)_*. Suppose both cones satisfy the universal property: every oriented cone from a test topos has a compatible lift, unique up to a unique isomorphism respecting its two projection comparisons. Then there exists a compatible comparison h:Q→P with h.direct an equivalence. For this comparison every other compatible h2 has a unique isomorphism of direct images respecting both projection comparisons.

source.place: ILO XI Theorem 1.4 and Definition 1.7; Lean: lean/Sheaf/CategoryTheory/Sites/OrientedProductUniversalComparison.lean

proof.text: Apply the two universal properties to the opposite cones to get h:Q→P and k:P→Q, with compatible projection isomorphisms. The pasted orientation for either composite is the iterated paste; expand the definition and use naturality and associativity to verify this componentwise. The identities are compatible cones as well.

Apply universal uniqueness to the composites and identities. Composing their two isomorphisms to a common chosen lift gives k.direct⋙h.direct≅id_P and id_Q≅h.direct⋙k.direct. Functor.IsEquivalence.mk' constructs the equivalence of h.direct. The unique projection-compatible isomorphism to another h2 is the uniqueness clause of the original universal property.

proof_origin.place: ILO XI Theorem 1.4 and Definition 1.7: the comparison maps in both directions have composites uniquely isomorphic to identities.

lean.statement:
theorem universalComparison
    (hP : IsGrothendieckTopos.{u} P) (hQ : IsGrothendieckTopos.{u} Q)
    (hp : IsUniversal.{u, u + 1, u} f g p₁ p₂ τ)
    (hq : IsUniversal.{u, u + 1, u} f g q₁ q₂ σ) :
    ∃ (h : GeometricMorphism Q P)
      (α : (h.comp p₁).direct ≅ q₁.direct) (β : (h.comp p₂).direct ≅ q₂.direct),
      paste f g p₁ p₂ τ h q₁ q₂ α β = σ ∧ h.direct.IsEquivalence ∧
      ∀ (h' : GeometricMorphism Q P)
        (α' : (h'.comp p₁).direct ≅ q₁.direct) (β' : (h'.comp p₂).direct ≅ q₂.direct),
        paste f g p₁ p₂ τ h' q₁ q₂ α' β' = σ →
        ∃! γ : h.direct ≅ h'.direct,
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight γ p₁.direct ≪≫ α' = α ∧
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight γ p₂.direct ≪≫ β' = β
